headline: Letter to the Editor: 'Grocery Store Music Is Absolutely Brainwashing You'
subheadline: Local Quantum Coffee enthusiast presents 'evidence' of subliminal cheese messaging
summary: A passionate letter claims supermarket background music contains hidden frequencies designed to influence purchasing decisions.
content:
**Letter to the Editor**

Dear Editor,

I write to you today as a concerned citizen who has spent the last 847 hours researching what I can only describe as the greatest consumer manipulation scandal of our time: grocery store music is brainwashing you to buy cheese.

Yes, cheese.

It began three months ago when I noticed something strange at SaveMart. Every time that soft jazz started playing, I found myself in the dairy aisle. Not walking toward it—just suddenly there, holding a block of cheddar I didn't need.

Coincidence? I thought so too. Then I started tracking my receipts.

Over 47 shopping trips, I purchased cheese during "muzak hours" 94% of the time, compared to only 23% during silent morning shopping. The correlation is undeniable. The cheese wants you to buy it, and it has weaponized smooth jazz to achieve its goals.

I attempted to discuss my findings with the SaveMart manager, who asked me to leave. I attempted to discuss them with my therapist, who also asked me to leave. I attempted to discuss them with the barista at The Underground, who made me a Quantum Coffee and said "that tracks, actually."

The coffee helped me think more clearly. I realized the problem goes deeper than one store. This is systemic. Big Dairy has infiltrated our soundscapes.

I urge your readers: wear headphones. Play your own music. The cheese cannot reach you if you cannot hear its siren song.

Stay vigilant,
Derek Patterson
Quantum Coffee Customer of the Month (Three Months Running)
